pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are 0 and 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item(); 'AC-2' test checks ★ only on the starred item.
'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and checks only those are listed in id order via ORDER BY id.
'AC-4' test covers / and /?show=all with the full list in id order.
'AC-5' test asserts both link anchors. The test is real evidence. The late spec edit to this item is a separate high finding.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred; 'AC-7' test asserts it. The traffic-config check was updated to accept a query string.

findings.what: Commit eee5e93 'Follow-up edits' edits AC-5 after the owner's go (2026-10-12). It splices '— verified by review: checked by hand' into the middle of the sentence, and the item now reads garbled. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for the change. 'Checked by hand' is also not a followable review step. The item already has a test, so the marker is unnecessary.
findings.fix: Revert the edit to AC-5. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but a later commit changed AC-5 in the spec after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or state the change and the owner's approval in the PR.

lenses.note: The spec exists and the code follows its decisions: order unchanged, query parameter, GET-only.
All 7 AC items and all 4 state rows have tests. The late AC-5 edit is a finding.
Tests assert rendered behaviour and states. I could not run the suite here (the Workers runtime is needed); CI is expected to run it.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The traffic-config check and its test were updated.
The show value is validated with Object.hasOwn, titles are HTML-escaped, and the SQL is static. No defects found.
The query input is allow-listed and output is escaped. The traffic-config check still rejects spaces and '#'.
The change renders only minimal server-side HTML (a nav link and list); there are no UI component, CSS or styling files.
